subject.title: fix(gateway-client): bound websocket opening handshake waits

question: Should the existing gateway preauth budget also become the fail-closed deadline for the WebSocket HTTP/TLS opening upgrade?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and contract-aligned, but it intentionally converts a previously unbounded transport phase into an upgrade-visible timeout for slow remote ingress.

options.title: Prove and land shared deadline
options.body: Keep the current design after adding delayed-success or live remote proof that a raised configured budget permits a slow but valid upgrade.

options.title: Accept loopback proof
options.body: Land with the submitted production loopback evidence and accept that unusually slow remote ingress may need the existing timeout setting raised.

options.title: Keep opening wait unbounded
options.body: Decline the fail-closed boundary and retain the current possibility of indefinitely stuck gateway clients.

recommendation.title: Prove and land shared deadline
recommendation.body: Keep the current design after adding delayed-success or live remote proof that a raised configured budget permits a slow but valid upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: The package extraction and shared timeout architecture both trace to this owner, making them the strongest routing candidate for the boundary decision.
